Listen to this article Share The Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC) has secured a Federal High Court order to freeze a bank account belonging to Yili Fu Liang Trading Co. Ltd over allegations of conspiracy and stealing involving N1.065 billion allegedly transferred from Renmoney Microfinance Bank through unauthorised electronic transactions. The order, granted by Yelim Bogoro, Justice of the Federal High Court in Lagos on Friday, October 16, 2026, followed an ex parte application filed by the anti-graft agency as part of its ongoing investigation into the alleged banking fraud. The commission also sought and obtained orders to place six Bank Verification Numbers (BVNs) on a watchlist pending the conclusion of investigations or possible prosecution. The case, marked FHC/LAG/MISC/1392/2026, arose from a petition submitted to the EFCC by Blackwood Law on behalf of Renmoney Microfinance Bank Limited, following a reported electronic banking incident on September 18, 2026. According to the EFCC, the petition, received on September 21, alleged that unauthorised transfers amounting to N1,065,500,000 were carried out through the microfinance bank’s application environment. In an affidavit supporting the application, Gbolahan Olabayo Dada, an EFCC investigating officer attached to the Bank Fraud Section, said the suspicious transactions occurred between approximately 4:52 p.m. and 8:00 p.m. on the day of the incident. The affidavit stated that 12 transactions were identified during the period, with the bank’s preliminary review estimating its financial exposure at N1.065 billion. Dada said preliminary investigations indicated that the funds were transferred to beneficiary accounts bearing the name Yili Fu Liang Trading Co. Ltd and linked to a collection account operated through Kora Payment Network. Investigators reportedly identified nine tranches of inflows, totalling N1,065,500,000, into the collection account on September 18. The investigating officer said preliminary findings suggested that the account holders did not have corresponding funds in their accounts before the alleged incident, raising concerns about the origin and movement of the money. He argued that freezing the account was necessary to preserve the funds while investigators continued examining the transactions and the possible involvement of the beneficiaries. The EFCC’s application specifically requested an order authorising it to direct the manager of the account identified in the court filings to freeze the funds pending the conclusion of investigations or possible prosecution. The account, held in the name of Yili Fu Liang, was reportedly linked to a virtual collection account maintained through Kora Payment Network with a new-generation bank. The commission also requested that six BVNs be placed on a watchlist to facilitate its investigation into the alleged fraud and prevent the possible dissipation of funds connected to the transactions. According to the affidavit, preliminary checks on the BVN portal and account-opening documents allegedly linked the holders of the six BVNs to Yili Fu Liang Trading Co. Ltd. Dada further alleged that the individuals behind the company were Nigerian nationals operating under the umbrella of a Chinese company. He said the individuals needed to be brought in for questioning as investigators sought to establish their respective roles in the transactions. The commission maintained that the requested orders were necessary to preserve the funds and prevent their possible dissipation while investigations into the allegations of stealing and money laundering continued. Moving the application, Z.B. Atiku, counsel to the EFCC, relied on the affidavit and the provisions of Section 44(2)(k) of the 1999 Constitution, as amended, Sections 26 and 28 of the EFCC Act, as well as the inherent jurisdiction of the court. After listening to the commission’s submissions, Bogoro granted the reliefs sought. The court subsequently adjourned the matter until January 19, 2027, for a report on the progress of the investigation.
